sourceHtml:
AI agents and applications that answer questions about recent events, product releases, prices, or regulations need information newer than their model’s training data. Until now, Web Search on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore delivered that information to agents through AgentCore Gateway, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. That means creating a gateway and a web search target and calling the tool from an MCP client. The setup fits platform teams that share one search policy across many agents, but it’s more than you need when your own code only requires search results.

Today, we’re announcing the Web Search API on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. With it, your own code can search the web with a single API call. It returns ranked results from a web index that Amazon operates, each with a text extract and, when available, the page title, URL, and publication time. You call it from the AWS SDKs or the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI), signed with the same AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) credentials you use for your other AWS services. There are no resources to create first. Authenticate, call, and get results. Use it in an application, an agent loop you write yourself, or a data pipeline.

Why a standalone API?

The AgentCore Gateway is the recommended path for most agentic workloads. It gives agents one secure Model Context Protocol (MCP) endpoint that combines web search with your other tools. It also handles inbound and outbound authentication, semantic tool selection, and optional MCP sessions. But developers told us they also need a lower-level integration point for scenarios where the gateway is not the right fit:

  • Custom orchestration frameworks – Developers building their own agent loops, or using frameworks like LangChain or LlamaIndex, want to call web search directly as a tool within their orchestration logic rather than routing through a gateway.
  • Non-agent use cases – Not every application that needs web grounding is an agent. Search-powered dashboards, fact-checking pipelines, content enrichment workflows, and monitoring systems all benefit from real-time web results without requiring agent infrastructure.
  • Tighter control over the request lifecycle – Some developers want to manage retries, caching, and error handling themselves rather than delegating to the gateway.
  • Simpler integration for existing applications – Applications that already have their own API layer can call the Web Search API directly, adding web grounding without adopting the full AgentCore Gateway stack.

The Web Search API complements the gateway. It runs on the same search infrastructure that powers Alexa+, Kiro, Quick, and other Amazon products, with the same quality and compliance posture, exposed as a direct API operation.

How it works

The Web Search API is the InvokeWebSearch operation on the bedrock-agentcore data plane, the same endpoint that other AgentCore tools such as AgentCore Browser, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, use. Requests are signed with AWS Signature Version 4 (SigV4) from your standard AWS credentials, so there’s no API key or secret to manage.

Figure 1: How a Web Search API request flows

The numbered steps are:

  1. Your application calls InvokeWebSearch with the AWS SDKs or the AWS CLI, which sign the request with SigV4 using its AWS credentials. From a virtual private cloud (VPC), the call can go through an interface VPC endpoint.
  2. The API checks with AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) that the caller has bedrock-agentcore:InvokeWebSearch on the AWS managed web search tool.
  3. The API applies the filters in the request: the domains to include or exclude and the publication time range.
  4. The API searches a web index that Amazon operates. Queries are served inside AWS and aren’t sent to a third-party search engine.
  5. The API returns up to maxResults ranked results, each with a text extract and, when available, the page title, URL, and publication time.

The calling identity needs one IAM permission on an AWS managed resource. It’s the same action and resource that a gateway’s service role uses for web search, so one policy covers both routes. For details, see Grant permission to call the API.

{
    "Version": "2012-10-17",
    "Statement": [
        {
            "Sid": "InvokeWebSearch",
            "Effect": "Allow",
            "Action": "bedrock-agentcore:InvokeWebSearch",
            "Resource": "arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:us-west-2:aws:tool/web-search.v1"
        }
    ]
}

A first search request

The following example searches two trusted domains for pages published in 2026, in the US West (Oregon) Region (us-west-2), with the AWS SDK for Python (Boto3):

import boto3

client = boto3.client("bedrock-agentcore", region_name="us-west-2")

response = client.invoke_web_search(
    webSearchId="web-search.v1",
    searchQuery="multi-region EKS cluster deployment best practices",
    maxResults=10,
    filters={
        "domainFilter": {"include": ["aws.amazon.com", "kubernetes.io"]},
        "publishedDateFilter": {"publishedAfter": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"},
    },
)

for result in response["results"]:
    print(result.get("publishedAt"), result.get("title"), result.get("url"))

Every result has a text extract. The title, URL, and publication date come back when the index has them, so read them with get. One result from a live call, shortened:

{
    "title": "One Amazon EKS, many edges: How to choose your edge container strategy on AWS",
    "url": "https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/containers/one-amazon-eks-many-edges-how-to-choose-your-edge-container-strategy-on-aws/",
    "text": "Separate the standard from the deployment model Choosing the wrong platform isn't really the issue. ...",
    "publishedAt": "2026-09-25T15:52:00Z"
}

That’s the full integration. If your code runs on AWS Lambda, Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS), Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2), or Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS), the execution role provides credentials automatically. Add the permission to that role, and the same code runs unchanged.

Key API features

  • Domain filtering – Include or exclude specific domains to scope search results to trusted sources (for example, only aws.amazon.com and kubernetes.io for an assistant focused on AWS). Each list holds up to 100 domain names, and a root domain also matches its subdomains.
  • Date filtering – Restrict results to a publication time range with publishedAfter and publishedBefore, given as RFC 3339 date-times in UTC such as 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z. Both bounds are inclusive.
  • Configurable result count – Request between 1 and 25 results per query. If you don’t set maxResults, the API returns up to 25. The search text, searchQuery, can be up to 200 characters.
  • Results with text extracts – Each result includes a text extract and, when available, the page title, URL, and publication time, ready to feed into your model’s context window.

Getting started in under 5 minutes

Here are two ways to get a first result:

Option 1: AWS CloudShell (no local setup)

  1. Open AWS CloudShell in your browser. It uses the credentials of your console session.
  2. Your role will have the bedrock-agentcore:InvokeWebSearch permission, from the preceding policy or from the broader AWS managed policy BedrockAgentCoreFullAccess.
  3. Run: 
    aws bedrock-agentcore invoke-web-search \
    --web-search-id web-search.v1 \
    --search-query "latest EKS features" \
    --max-results 5

Option 2: Local development

  1. Install the AWS CLI, or the AWS SDK for your language. For Python, use Boto3 1.43.127 or later.
  2. Create an IAM role with the preceding policy.
  3. Get credentials for that role: assume it from your application or an AWS CLI profile, or sign in with it through your identity provider.
  4. Run the preceding Python example, or call the API from any AWS SDK.

There’s no resource to create and no API key to manage. Authenticate, call, and get results.

Using the Web Search API with agent frameworks

The Web Search API fits naturally into popular agent frameworks. LangChain agents get it through the AgentCore web search tool in langchain-aws 1.9.3 and later:

from langchain.agents import create_agent
from langchain.chat_models import init_chat_model
from langchain_aws.tools import create_web_search_toolkit

toolkit, tools = create_web_search_toolkit(region="us-west-2")
model = init_chat_model("bedrock_converse:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5", region_name="us-west-2")
agent = create_agent(model, tools=tools, system_prompt="Cite the URL of every fact you use.")

The tool can also hold rules that the model can’t change, such as domains to exclude, a date floor, and a search budget. It returns its results as data that your code can check. For a complete example, see the daily dependency watch sample. It researches three package ecosystems in parallel with LangGraph, and checks every finding against its sources before it reports anything.

If you prefer to wrap the call yourself, a plain LangChain tool works too:

from langchain.tools import tool
import boto3
import json

client = boto3.client("bedrock-agentcore", region_name="us-west-2")

@tool
def web_search(query: str) -> str:
    """Search the web for current information."""
    response = client.invoke_web_search(
        webSearchId="web-search.v1",
        searchQuery=query,
        maxResults=5,
    )
    return json.dumps(response["results"], indent=2, default=str)

# Pass web_search to an agent, for example create_agent(model, tools=[web_search])

Without a framework, the WebSearchClient in the AgentCore Python SDK wraps the same call and returns results with parsed dates. langchain-aws 1.9.3 and the AgentCore Python SDK 1.26.0 add Web Search API support, so install those versions or later.

Enterprise controls, built in

Because the Web Search API uses standard IAM authentication, you get enterprise controls from the first call:

  • IAM policies. Grant or deny bedrock-agentcore:InvokeWebSearch per user, group, or role. Use service control policies (SCPs) to enforce guardrails across accounts.
  • AWS CloudTrail logging. CloudTrail records InvokeWebSearch requests as data events. Data events aren’t logged by default, so add an event selector for the AWS::BedrockAgentCore::WebSearch resource type to a trail or event data store. Events record the web search tool and maxResults, not the search text or filters. For details, see Log AgentCore Web Search API calls with AWS CloudTrail.
  • VPC support. Use AWS PrivateLink to route API calls over your private network rather than the public internet. For setup and endpoint policies, see Private connectivity with AWS PrivateLink later in this post.
  • Compliance. For a list of compliance programs that cover AgentCore, see Compliance validation for Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.
  • Searches stay in AWS. Queries are served from a web index that Amazon operates and aren’t sent to a third-party search engine.
  • Acceptable use. For details, see the Web Search API Acceptable Use documentation.

Quotas apply per account. For the defaults and how to request an increase, see Quotas for Amazon Bedrock AgentCore.

By default, each account can send up to 10 requests per second in each Region, and you can request an increase. For details, see AgentCore Web Search Service Quotas.

Private connectivity with AWS PrivateLink

Agents and pipelines that handle sensitive data often run in private subnets with no route to the internet. With AWS PrivateLink, that code can call the Web Search API through an interface VPC endpoint in your VPC. Traffic between your VPC and the API stays on the AWS network, and you don’t need an internet gateway, a NAT gateway, or a proxy to reach it.

Figure 2: Calling the Web Search API through AWS PrivateLink

The numbered steps are:

  1. Your application calls InvokeWebSearch at the API’s standard Regional name. With private DNS, that name resolves to the interface endpoint in your subnet.
  2. The endpoint policy applies, and the request reaches the API over the AWS network.
  3. The API checks with IAM that the caller has bedrock-agentcore:InvokeWebSearch, including any aws:SourceVpce condition.
  4. The API applies the request’s filters and searches the Amazon-operated web index.
  5. The results return through the endpoint to your application.

To set it up, create an interface endpoint for the AgentCore data plane service, com.amazonaws.<Region>.bedrock-agentcore, in each VPC and Region that calls the API, and turn on private DNS:

aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint \
    --region us-west-2 \
    --vpc-id vpc-0123456789abcdef0 \
    --vpc-endpoint-type Interface \
    --service-name com.amazonaws.us-west-2.bedrock-agentcore \
    --subnet-ids subnet-0123456789abcdef0 subnet-0fedcba9876543210 \
    --security-group-ids sg-0123456789abcdef0 \
    --private-dns-enabled

With private DNS turned on, the API’s standard Regional name, bedrock-agentcore.us-west-2.amazonaws.com, resolves to the endpoint’s private IP addresses inside your VPC. The Boto3 and AWS CLI examples in this post run unchanged, with no endpoint URL to set. The endpoint’s security group must allow inbound HTTPS (port 443) from the resources that call the API.

PrivateLink also gives you controls on top of IAM:

  1. Endpoint policies – A VPC endpoint policy applies to InvokeWebSearch requests in addition to your IAM policies, so you decide which principals can search through the endpoint. The same endpoint also carries the other AgentCore data plane APIs, such as AgentCore runtime, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Memory, Identity, Browser, and Code Interpreter. If workloads in the VPC call them too, add statements that allow those calls. The following policy lets only one role call the API through the endpoint: 
    {
    "Effect": "Allow",
    "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/WebSearchAppRole" },
    "Action": "bedrock-agentcore:InvokeWebSearch",
    "Resource": "arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:us-west-2:aws:tool/web-search.v1"
}
  2. Require the private path – Add an aws:SourceVpce condition to the IAM policy that grants the permission. The role can then search only through your endpoint, and the same call from outside the VPC is denied: 
    {
    "Effect": "Allow",
    "Action": "bedrock-agentcore:InvokeWebSearch",
    "Resource": "arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:us-west-2:aws:tool/web-search.v1",
    "Condition": { "StringEquals": { "aws:SourceVpce": "vpce-0123456789abcdef0" } }
}
  3. Network-level control – Security groups and subnet placement decide which instances, containers, and functions can reach the endpoint at all.

PrivateLink works the same way in every Region where the Web Search API is available. Interface endpoints are billed at standard AWS PrivateLink pricing. For details, see Call AgentCore Web Search through AWS PrivateLink.

Try it in the console

You can try the Web Search API in the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore console before you write any code. In the navigation pane, under Connections, choose Web Search.

Figure 3: Web Search in the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore console

  1. Configure. In the Configure panel, set:
    1. Max results: how many results each query returns, from 1–25. The console starts at 10.
    2. Published date: a date range in YYYY/MM/DD format. Only results published inside it come back. Leave it empty to include results from any date.
    3. Domain filtering: up to 100 domains to include and up to 100 to exclude. Choose View and manage domains to edit the lists.
  2. Test. Enter a query of up to 200 characters in the Test Web Search API panel. Each query calls the Web Search API with your settings. The panel shows how many results came back and how long the call took. For each result it shows the title, a text snippet, the publication date and the source URL. Figure 4 shows a search for “How do I set up Amazon S3 lifecycle rules?” with results limited to aws.amazon.com and docs.aws.amazon.com.

Figure 4: A test search with included domains

  1. Integrate. When the results look right, you have two options:
    1. Generate code snippet: get code that calls the API with the same settings, ready to paste into your agent or application.
    2. Create gateway target: add Web Search as a tool on an AgentCore Gateway, so agents can call it through MCP.

The console signs each call with your own IAM identity, so your role needs the bedrock-agentcore:InvokeWebSearch permission.

When to use the API compared to the gateway

Scenario Recommended path
Building agents with MCP-compatible tools AgentCore Gateway
Several tools behind one MCP endpoint, with optional MCP sessions AgentCore Gateway
One administrator source policy for many agents and teams AgentCore Gateway
MCP clients that need search, such as Claude with the AWS Web Search connector AgentCore Gateway
Custom orchestration Web Search API
Non-agent use cases (dashboards, pipelines) Web Search API
Want direct control over retries and caching Web Search API
Adding web search to an existing application Web Search API

Both paths search the same index. They differ in a few ways. A gateway can also authorize callers with a JSON Web Token (JWT), while the API authorizes with IAM only. On a gateway, an administrator can set domain lists on the target that apply to every request without the calling agent seeing them. With the API, each request carries its own filters. The field names differ too: the API takes searchQuery, publishedAfter, and publishedBefore, and the gateway’s MCP tool takes query, from, and to. For more guidance, see Choose between the API and the Gateway connector.

Pricing

The Web Search API meters to the same usage type as the gateway connector, so it’s billed at the Web Search rate of $7 per 1,000 queries. Because no gateway is involved, there are no gateway charges. For details, see Amazon Bedrock AgentCore pricing.

Availability

The Web Search API is available in the US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), US West (Oregon), Europe (Ireland), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), and Asia Pacific (Sydney) Regions. For the current list, see Supported AWS Regions.

Get started

Use the following resources to help you get started.

  • Web Search API documentation
  • Web Search on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
  • InvokeWebSearch API reference

About the authors

translation.html:
回答近期事件、产品发布、价格或法规相关问题的 AI 智能体和应用，需要比模型训练数据更新的信息。此前，Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 上的网页搜索通过 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 的一项功能 AgentCore Gateway 向智能体提供这些信息。这意味着需要创建网关和网页搜索目标，并从 MCP 客户端调用该工具。这种配置适合在多个智能体之间共享同一搜索策略的平台团队，但如果你自己的代码只需要搜索结果，这样的配置就超出了实际需要。

今天，我们宣布推出 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 上的 Web Search API。借助它，你自己的代码只需调用一次 API 即可搜索网页。它从 Amazon 运营的网页索引中返回经过排序的结果，每条结果都包含文本摘录，并在可用时提供页面标题、URL 和发布时间。你可以通过 AWS SDK 或 AWS Command Line Interface（AWS CLI）调用它，使用与其他 AWS 服务相同的 AWS Identity and Access Management（IAM）凭证对请求进行签名。无需预先创建任何资源。完成身份验证、发起调用，即可获取结果。你可以将它用于应用、自行编写的智能体循环或数据流水线。

为什么要提供独立 API？

对于大多数智能体工作负载，推荐使用 AgentCore Gateway。它为智能体提供一个安全的模型上下文协议（MCP）端点，将网页搜索与你的其他工具整合在一起。它还负责入站和出站身份验证、语义工具选择，以及可选的 MCP 会话。不过，开发者告诉我们，在网关不适用的场景中，他们也需要一个更底层的集成入口：

  • 自定义编排框架 – 自行构建智能体循环，或使用 LangChain、LlamaIndex 等框架的开发者，希望在编排逻辑中将网页搜索作为工具直接调用，而无需通过网关转发。
  • 非智能体用例 – 需要以网页信息为依据的应用并不都是智能体。搜索驱动的仪表板、事实核查流水线、内容丰富工作流和监控系统，都能从实时网页结果中获益，而无需智能体基础设施。
  • 更精细地控制请求生命周期 – 一些开发者希望自行管理重试、缓存和错误处理，而不是交由网关处理。
  • 让现有应用更容易集成 – 已经拥有自身 API 层的应用可以直接调用 Web Search API，无需采用完整的 AgentCore Gateway 技术栈，即可添加网页信息支撑能力。

Web Search API 是对网关的补充。它运行在为 Alexa+、Kiro、Quick 和其他 Amazon 产品提供支持的同一套搜索基础设施上，具有相同的质量和合规水平，并以可直接调用的 API 操作形式提供。

工作原理

Web Search API 是 bedrock-agentcore 数据平面上的 InvokeWebSearch 操作。Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 的 AgentCore Browser 等其他 AgentCore 工具也使用同一个端点。请求使用你的标准 AWS 凭证，通过 AWS Signature Version 4（SigV4）进行签名，因此无需管理 API 密钥或秘密凭证。

图 1：Web Search API 请求的处理流程

编号步骤如下：

  1. 你的应用通过 AWS SDK 或 AWS CLI 调用 InvokeWebSearch，后者使用应用的 AWS 凭证，通过 SigV4 对请求进行签名。从虚拟私有云（VPC）发起调用时，可以通过接口 VPC 端点进行。
  2. API 通过 AWS Identity and Access Management（IAM）检查调用方是否对 AWS 托管的网页搜索工具拥有 bedrock-agentcore:InvokeWebSearch 权限。
  3. API 应用请求中的筛选条件：要包含或排除的域名，以及发布时间范围。
  4. API 搜索由 Amazon 运营的网页索引。查询在 AWS 内部处理，不会发送给第三方搜索引擎。
  5. API 返回最多 maxResults 条经过排序的结果，每条结果都包含文本摘录，并在可用时提供页面标题、URL 和发布时间。

调用身份需要对一个 AWS 托管资源拥有一项 IAM 权限。这与网关服务角色用于网页搜索的操作和资源相同，因此同一份策略即可覆盖这两种调用路径。详情请参阅授予调用 API 的权限。

{
    "Version": "2012-10-17",
    "Statement": [
        {
            "Sid": "InvokeWebSearch",
            "Effect": "Allow",
            "Action": "bedrock-agentcore:InvokeWebSearch",
            "Resource": "arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:us-west-2:aws:tool/web-search.v1"
        }
    ]
}

首次搜索请求

以下示例使用 AWS SDK for Python（Boto3），在美国西部（俄勒冈）区域（us-west-2）搜索两个可信域名中于 2026 年发布的页面：

import boto3

client = boto3.client("bedrock-agentcore", region_name="us-west-2")

response = client.invoke_web_search(
    webSearchId="web-search.v1",
    searchQuery="multi-region EKS cluster deployment best practices",
    maxResults=10,
    filters={
        "domainFilter": {"include": ["aws.amazon.com", "kubernetes.io"]},
        "publishedDateFilter": {"publishedAfter": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"},
    },
)

for result in response["results"]:
    print(result.get("publishedAt"), result.get("title"), result.get("url"))

每条结果都有文本摘录。当索引包含标题、URL 和发布日期时，这些字段也会返回，因此请使用 get 读取它们。以下是一次实际调用返回的一条结果，内容经过缩短：

{
    "title": "One Amazon EKS, many edges: How to choose your edge container strategy on AWS",
    "url": "https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/containers/one-amazon-eks-many-edges-how-to-choose-your-edge-container-strategy-on-aws/",
    "text": "Separate the standard from the deployment model Choosing the wrong platform isn't really the issue. ...",
    "publishedAt": "2026-09-25T15:52:00Z"
}

这就是完整的集成过程。如果你的代码运行在 AWS Lambda、Amazon Elastic Container Service（Amazon ECS）、Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud（Amazon EC2） 或 Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service（Amazon EKS） 上，执行角色会自动提供凭证。为该角色添加权限后，同一份代码无需修改即可运行。

主要 API 功能

  • 域名筛选 – 包含或排除特定域名，将搜索结果限定在可信来源内（例如，专注于 AWS 的助手可以仅搜索 aws.amazon.com 和 kubernetes.io）。每个列表最多可包含 100 个域名，根域名也会匹配其子域名。
  • 日期筛选 – 使用 publishedAfter 和 publishedBefore 将结果限制在某个发布时间范围内，时间以 UTC 时区的 RFC 3339 日期时间格式指定，例如 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z。上下限均包含在范围内。
  • 可配置的结果数量 – 每次查询可请求 1 至 25 条结果。如果不设置 maxResults，API 最多返回 25 条。搜索文本 searchQuery 最长为 200 个字符。
  • 附带文本摘录的结果 – 每条结果都包含文本摘录，并在可用时提供页面标题、URL 和发布时间，可以直接放入模型的上下文窗口。

不到 5 分钟即可开始使用

以下是获取首个结果的两种方式：

方式 1：AWS CloudShell（无需本地配置）

  1. 在浏览器中打开 AWS CloudShell。它会使用你的控制台会话凭证。
  2. 你的角色将通过前述策略或权限范围更广的 AWS 托管策略 BedrockAgentCoreFullAccess，获得 bedrock-agentcore:InvokeWebSearch 权限。
  3. Run: 
    aws bedrock-agentcore invoke-web-search \
    --web-search-id web-search.v1 \
    --search-query "latest EKS features" \
    --max-results 5

方式 2：本地开发

  1. 安装 AWS CLI 或适用于你所用语言的 AWS SDK。对于 Python，请使用 Boto3 1.43.127 或更高版本。
  2. 使用前述策略创建 IAM 角色。
  3. 获取该角色的凭证：从应用或 AWS CLI 配置文件代入该角色，或通过身份提供商以该角色登录。
  4. 运行前述 Python 示例，或通过任意 AWS SDK 调用 API。

无需创建资源，也无需管理 API 密钥。完成身份验证、发起调用，即可获取结果。

在智能体框架中使用 Web Search API

Web Search API 可以自然地融入常用智能体框架。LangChain 智能体可以通过 langchain-aws 1.9.3 及更高版本中的 AgentCore 网页搜索工具使用它：

from langchain.agents import create_agent
from langchain.chat_models import init_chat_model
from langchain_aws.tools import create_web_search_toolkit

toolkit, tools = create_web_search_toolkit(region="us-west-2")
model = init_chat_model("bedrock_converse:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5", region_name="us-west-2")
agent = create_agent(model, tools=tools, system_prompt="Cite the URL of every fact you use.")

该工具还可以保存模型无法更改的规则，例如要排除的域名、最早日期限制和搜索预算。它以数据形式返回结果，供你的代码检查。完整示例请参阅每日依赖监测示例。该示例使用 LangGraph 并行研究三个软件包生态系统，并在报告任何发现之前，逐一对照来源进行核查。

如果你更愿意自行封装调用，普通的 LangChain 工具也可以：

from langchain.tools import tool
import boto3
import json

client = boto3.client("bedrock-agentcore", region_name="us-west-2")

@tool
def web_search(query: str) -> str:
    """Search the web for current information."""
    response = client.invoke_web_search(
        webSearchId="web-search.v1",
        searchQuery=query,
        maxResults=5,
    )
    return json.dumps(response["results"], indent=2, default=str)

# Pass web_search to an agent, for example create_agent(model, tools=[web_search])

如果不使用框架，AgentCore Python SDK 中的 WebSearchClient 封装了相同的调用，并返回已解析日期的结果。langchain-aws 1.9.3 和 AgentCore Python SDK 1.26.0 添加了对 Web Search API 的支持，因此请安装这些版本或更高版本。

内置企业级控制

由于 Web Search API 使用标准 IAM 身份验证，你从第一次调用起就能使用企业级控制：

  • IAM 策略。按用户、用户组或角色授予或拒绝 bedrock-agentcore:InvokeWebSearch 权限。使用服务控制策略（SCP）在多个账户之间强制实施防护规则。
  • AWS CloudTrail 日志记录。CloudTrail 将 InvokeWebSearch 请求记录为数据事件。默认情况下不记录数据事件，因此需要为跟踪或事件数据存储添加针对 AWS::BedrockAgentCore::WebSearch 资源类型的事件选择器。事件记录网页搜索工具和 maxResults，不会记录搜索文本或筛选条件。详情请参阅使用 AWS CloudTrail 记录 AgentCore Web Search API 调用。
  • VPC 支持。使用 AWS PrivateLink，通过你的私有网络而非公共互联网路由 API 调用。有关配置和端点策略，请参阅本文后面的“通过 AWS PrivateLink 实现私有连接”。
  • 合规性。有关涵盖 AgentCore 的合规计划列表，请参阅 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 的合规性验证。
  • 搜索始终在 AWS 内部进行。查询由 Amazon 运营的网页索引提供服务，不会发送给第三方搜索引擎。
  • 可接受使用。详情请参阅 Web Search API 可接受使用文档。

配额按账户生效。有关默认配额和申请提高配额的方法，请参阅 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 配额。

默认情况下，每个账户在每个区域每秒最多可以发送 10 个请求，你可以申请提高此限额。详情请参阅 AgentCore Web Search 服务配额。

通过 AWS PrivateLink 实现私有连接

处理敏感数据的智能体和流水线通常运行在没有互联网路由的私有子网中。借助 AWS PrivateLink，这些代码可以通过 VPC 中的接口 VPC 端点调用 Web Search API。VPC 与 API 之间的流量始终留在 AWS 网络内，无需互联网网关、NAT 网关或代理即可访问该 API。

图 2：通过 AWS PrivateLink 调用 Web Search API

编号步骤如下：

  1. 你的应用通过 API 的标准区域域名调用 InvokeWebSearch。启用私有 DNS 后，该域名会解析到你子网中的接口端点。
  2. 端点策略生效，请求通过 AWS 网络到达 API。
  3. API 通过 IAM 检查调用方是否拥有 bedrock-agentcore:InvokeWebSearch 权限，包括是否满足任何 aws:SourceVpce 条件。
  4. API 应用请求中的筛选条件，并搜索 Amazon 运营的网页索引。
  5. 结果通过端点返回你的应用。

要进行配置，请在调用 API 的每个 VPC 和区域中，为 AgentCore 数据平面服务 com.amazonaws.<Region>.bedrock-agentcore 创建接口端点，并启用私有 DNS：

aws ec2 create-vpc-endpoint \
    --region us-west-2 \
    --vpc-id vpc-0123456789abcdef0 \
    --vpc-endpoint-type Interface \
    --service-name com.amazonaws.us-west-2.bedrock-agentcore \
    --subnet-ids subnet-0123456789abcdef0 subnet-0fedcba9876543210 \
    --security-group-ids sg-0123456789abcdef0 \
    --private-dns-enabled

启用私有 DNS 后，API 的标准区域域名 bedrock-agentcore.us-west-2.amazonaws.com 会在你的 VPC 内解析为端点的私有 IP 地址。本文中的 Boto3 和 AWS CLI 示例无需修改即可运行，也无需设置端点 URL。端点的安全组必须允许来自调用 API 的资源的入站 HTTPS 流量（端口 443）。

除了 IAM，PrivateLink 还提供以下控制：

  1. Endpoint policies – A VPC endpoint policy applies to InvokeWebSearch requests in addition to your IAM policies, so you decide which principals can search through the endpoint. The same endpoint also carries the other AgentCore data plane APIs, such as AgentCore runtime, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, Memory, Identity, Browser, and Code Interpreter. If workloads in the VPC call them too, add statements that allow those calls. The following policy lets only one role call the API through the endpoint: 
    {
    "Effect": "Allow",
    "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/WebSearchAppRole" },
    "Action": "bedrock-agentcore:InvokeWebSearch",
    "Resource": "arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:us-west-2:aws:tool/web-search.v1"
}
  2. Require the private path – Add an aws:SourceVpce condition to the IAM policy that grants the permission. The role can then search only through your endpoint, and the same call from outside the VPC is denied: 
    {
    "Effect": "Allow",
    "Action": "bedrock-agentcore:InvokeWebSearch",
    "Resource": "arn:aws:bedrock-agentcore:us-west-2:aws:tool/web-search.v1",
    "Condition": { "StringEquals": { "aws:SourceVpce": "vpce-0123456789abcdef0" } }
}
  3. 网络级控制 – 安全组和子网部署位置决定哪些实例、容器和函数能够访问端点。

在 Web Search API 可用的每个区域，PrivateLink 的工作方式都相同。接口端点按标准 AWS PrivateLink 定价收费。详情请参阅通过 AWS PrivateLink 调用 AgentCore Web Search。

在控制台中试用

在编写任何代码之前，你可以先在 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 控制台中试用 Web Search API。在导航窗格的 Connections 下，选择 Web Search。

图 3：Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 控制台中的 Web Search

  1. Configure. In the Configure panel, set:
    1. 最大结果数：每次查询返回的结果数量，范围为 1–25。控制台的初始值为 10。
    2. 发布日期：以 YYYY/MM/DD 格式指定的日期范围。仅返回在该范围内发布的结果。留空则包含任意日期的结果。
    3. 域名筛选：最多可包含 100 个域名，并排除 100 个域名。选择 View and manage domains 编辑列表。
  2. 测试。在 Test Web Search API 面板中输入最长 200 个字符的查询。每次查询都会按你的设置调用 Web Search API。面板会显示返回的结果数量和调用耗时。对于每条结果，面板会显示标题、文本片段、发布日期和来源 URL。图 4 展示了对“如何设置 Amazon S3 生命周期规则？”的搜索，结果限定在 aws.amazon.com 和 docs.aws.amazon.com。

图 4：指定包含域名的测试搜索

  1. Integrate. When the results look right, you have two options:
    1. 生成代码片段：获取使用相同设置调用 API 的代码，可直接粘贴到你的智能体或应用中。
    2. 创建网关目标：将 Web Search 作为工具添加到 AgentCore Gateway，使智能体能够通过 MCP 调用它。

控制台使用你自己的 IAM 身份对每次调用进行签名，因此你的角色需要拥有 bedrock-agentcore:InvokeWebSearch 权限。

何时使用 API，何时使用网关

场景 推荐路径
使用兼容 MCP 的工具构建智能体 AgentCore Gateway
通过一个 MCP 端点提供多个工具，并支持可选的 MCP 会话 AgentCore Gateway
为多个智能体和团队提供统一的管理员信源策略 AgentCore Gateway
需要搜索功能的 MCP 客户端，例如使用 AWS Web Search 连接器的 Claude AgentCore Gateway
自定义编排 Web Search API
非智能体用例（仪表板、流水线） Web Search API
希望直接控制重试和缓存 Web Search API
为现有应用添加网页搜索 Web Search API

两种路径搜索的是同一个索引，但它们在几个方面有所不同。网关还可以使用 JSON Web Token（JWT）对调用方进行授权，而 API 仅使用 IAM 进行授权。在网关上，管理员可以在目标上设置适用于每个请求的域名列表，调用的智能体无法看到这些列表。使用 API 时，每个请求自行携带筛选条件。字段名称也有所不同：API 接受 searchQuery、publishedAfter 和 publishedBefore，网关的 MCP 工具接受 query、from 和 to。更多指导请参阅在 API 和 Gateway 连接器之间进行选择。

定价

Web Search API 按照与网关连接器相同的用量类型计量，因此按 Web Search 的费率收费，即每 1,000 次查询 7 美元。由于不涉及网关，因此没有网关费用。详情请参阅 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 定价。

可用区域

Web Search API 已在美国东部（弗吉尼亚北部）、美国东部（俄亥俄）、美国西部（俄勒冈）、欧洲（爱尔兰）、亚太地区（东京）和亚太地区（悉尼）区域推出。当前列表请参阅支持的 AWS 区域。
